question: I'm a sophomore thinking about switching into the biology major. What are all the required courses and how many credits is the major total?

question: can intro to stats count toward the psychology major or do psych majors have to take a different stats class

body.answer:

The catalog does not identify a course by the exact name “Intro to Stats,” so I can’t verify whether a different course with that title would count. question: what gen ed categories do i still need to fill if ive already done comp 1 and a math class

body.answer:
Ramapo students must complete all four keystone courses—First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities—one course in each keystone category (Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, Quantitative Reasoning), and one course in two of the three distribution categories (Culture & Creativity; Systems, Sustainability, & Society; Values & Ethics). [6] If by “Comp 1” you mean Critical Reading & Writing I, that does not establish completion of required Critical Reading & Writing 102. [3][6]

If your math course was MATH 100T, 101, 104, 106, 108, or 110, the catalog lists it as Quantitative Reasoning (GEQR). [14] In that case, based only on the two courses you mentioned, the other listed requirements to check are First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, Studies in the Arts & Humanities, Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and two distribution categories. [6] I can’t verify your individual degree audit or whether your specific courses were applied to it.

For an individual check, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising), D-207, success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441. Students who have completed 64 credits must have completed their Critical Reading and Writing and college-level math general education courses or face a registration hold. [13]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: whats the difference between developmental psych and child psych, are they the same class

body.answer:
No. They are separate 4-credit courses, and both require PSYC 101 INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY. [2][3]

PSYC 241 DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOLOGY covers basic processes of lifespan human development, drawing on multiple theoretical standpoints and exploring influences and key debates in lifespan development. [2]

PSYC 263 CHILD PSYCHOLOGY focuses on children’s growth, development, and behavior, especially infancy and early childhood, including physical, intellectual, social, and emotional development and influences on behavior. [3]

In the Psychology BA (Bachelor of Arts), both count as options in “Category 3: Developmental - Select 1”; neither is required by itself. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC241) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC263)

question: what are the gen ed requirements at ramapo, like how many credits total and what categories

body.answer:
Ramapo describes General Education as ten courses, not a fixed credit total; the curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits.” [6][11] The ten-course structure is four keystone courses—First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities—plus one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning, and one course in two of three Distribution categories. [11]

For Fall 2026, the distribution categories are Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society; choose two. [10] Section 11 instead calls the third category Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and says at least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. The pages differ; section 10 says that starting Fall 2026 the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools. [10][11]

Critical Reading & Writing 102 and Quantitative Reasoning must be completed within the first 64 credits; the catalog also says students must complete general education reading/writing and mathematics requirements by 64 credits. [11][12] Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all Gen Ed requirements, as specified by the transfer and waiver policies. [7]

Sources: [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [12](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics)

question: What graduate programs does Ramapo offer? I'm specifically wondering if there is a master's in educational leadership or a master's in social work.

body.answer:
Ramapo’s listed graduate programs are: Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP); M.S. in Accounting (MSAC); Master of Business Administration (MBA); M.S. in Data Science (MSDS); M.S. in Nursing (MSN); M.A. in Special Education (MASE); Master of Social Work (MSW); M.S. in Applied Mathematics (MSAM); M.S. in Computer Science (MSCS); and Master of Public Policy. [4]
The list does not include a master’s in educational leadership. It does include the M.A. in Special Education, but that is a different program. [4]
Yes—Ramapo offers the Master of Social Work (MSW), in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. [1][4] The catalog specifies an Advanced Standing Track (30 credits) and a Traditional Track (60 credits). [1] The program is also published at the BSW level. [1]

question: How many total credits do you need to graduate with a bachelor's degree from Ramapo, and how many of those have to be taken at Ramapo as a transfer student?

body.answer:
Ramapo’s general minimum is 128 credits to graduate with a bachelor’s degree; some programs may require more. [4][7][11][12]

The pages differ on how many credits a transfer student must complete at Ramapo:
- Section 4 says students entering from a two-year college must complete at least 63 credits at Ramapo; those entering from a four-year college, at least 32. [4]
- Section 11 says all undergraduate students must complete at least 48 credits at Ramapo, including the final 32 in residence. [11]
- Sections 6 and 7 state a minimum of 32 credits at Ramapo; section 7 also says the final 32 must be completed in residence. [6][7]
- Section 12 likewise says at least 32 credits at Ramapo. [12]

Section 6 also requires at least half the requirements of a major, second major, or minor at Ramapo. [6] Check with the Registrar about which residency rule applies to you: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695. [11][12]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#undergraduate-residency-requirement1) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#graduation-requirements) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/)

question: For the nursing program, what are the prerequisite courses I would need to have done before I could start the nursing sequence?

body.answer:
For the **Nursing Generic BSN (Bachelor of Science in Nursing)**, the pre-nursing courses are: [2]
- **Math: choose 1:** MATH 108 Elementary Probability and Statistics or PSYC 242 Statistics. [2]
- **All science courses:** BIOL 212 Microbiology for Health Science Lecture and BIOL 212L Microbiology for Health Science Laboratory; BIOL 214 Anatomy and Physiology I Lecture and BIOL 214L Anatomy & Physiology I Lab; BIOL 216 Anatomy & Physiology II Lecture and BIOL 216L Anatomy & Physiology II Lab; CHEM 111 Principles of Chemistry Lecture and CHEM 111L Principles of Chem Lab/Recitat; PSYC 101 Introduction to Psychology. [2]

If you mean the **Nursing Accelerated BSN (Bachelor of Science in Nursing)**, its Bridge prerequisites are BIOL 212 and 212L, BIOL 214 and 214L, BIOL 216 and 216L, CHEM 111 and 111L, MATH 108, and PSYC 101. You must earn a grade of C+ or better in all Bridge courses to proceed to the Nursing courses. [1]

Both programs also publish Nursing MSN. [1][2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURA) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG)

question: What does CMPS 147 cover and what are its prereqs? I took an intro programming class at my community college and want to know if it's the same thing.

body.answer:
CMPS 147 COMPUTER SCIENCE I is 4 credits. It covers problem-solving with computers; computer systems; ANSI C++; algorithm design; program development, debugging, testing and documentation; variables, data types, expressions, selection, repetition, functions and arrays. Course fee required; Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR). [1]

Prerequisite: complete one of these courses: MATH 021, MATH 022, MATH 024, MATH 100T, MATH 101, MATH 104, MATH 108, MATH 110 or MATH 121; OR achieve the required score on one test: ACCUPLACER Quantitative Reasoning (258), ACCUPLACER Advanced Algebra and Functions (260), ACT Composite (26) or SAT MATH (580). [1]

The catalog does not establish whether your community-college intro programming class is equivalent to CMPS 147. INFO 233 is a different Ramapo course: it covers programming with a modern language, structured event-driven programs for business problems, programming constructs, object-oriented programming, algorithms and problem-solving. [2] For transfer coursework, credit may transfer if Ramapo offers a comparable course or discipline, you earn at least a C, and the college is regionally accredited. [6]

For advice about meeting prerequisites or registration, contact the Science, Nursing and Health school, which offers CMPS 147. If you are a transfer student who fulfilled a prerequisite but cannot register, contact that academic school; if you prove you satisfied it, the unit secretary may place an override, then register in Experience: https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/. [4] For transfer-credit questions: Registrar, reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224. [4][6]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CMPS147) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/INFO233) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/)

question: Could you explain how the general education requirements are structured at Ramapo? I want to know which categories I'd need to fill coming in as a transfer.

body.answer:
Ramapo’s General Education curriculum has four keystone courses—First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities—plus one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Critical Reading & Writing 102 and Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits. You also take one course in two of three distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. [5]

For transfers, the categories still required depend on your credits and degree. Transfers with at least 48 credits must fulfill Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and one course in two distribution categories; they are waived from First Year Seminar, Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities. [7, 9] Transfers with an A.A. or A.S. from a New Jersey community college are waived from General Education after submitting a final official transcript with the conferred degree; an A.A.S. does not qualify for a full waiver, and courses are evaluated individually. [10] Other transfers may transfer or be waived from some or all requirements under the stated policies. [8]

The pages differ on the distribution-category label: section 5 says “Systems, Sustainability, & Society,” while section 6 lists “Social Systems and Society.” Section 5 says at least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than your major’s; section 6 says, starting Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools. [5, 6]

I don’t have verified information about your evaluated credits or which requirements remain for you personally. During academic advisement, students are advised of applicable waivers and remaining courses. [7, 9] Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207. Contact Admissions about transfer-credit policy: admissions@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7300. [10]

Sources: [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/)

question: Does a statistics course count toward the gen ed math requirement, or does it have to be something like college algebra or calc?

body.answer:
Yes—MATH 108 Elementary Probability and Statistics counts: the catalog lists it as Gen Ed 18–Quantitative Reasoning (GEQR) [16]. The Testing Center says MATH 101, 104, 106, 108, or PHIL 106 are college-level courses that meet your General Education and/or major math requirement [14]. The catalog also lists MATH 121 Calculus I as GEQR [16], so it does not have to be calculus. But not every statistics course counts: MATH 353 Statistics has no Gen Ed attribute [3]. See the approved General Education courses in the College Catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [8].

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MATH353) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/post-testing/) [16](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: what's the suggested 4 year plan for the computer science major, specifically what should be taken in the first two semesters

body.answer:
The Computer Science BS (Bachelor of Science) recommended plan is for students admitted during the 2026–2027 academic year [1]. Its first two semesters are: [1]

**First Year, Fall Semester — total 16 credits** [1]
- CMPS 147 - COMPUTER SCIENCE I (4)
- Quantitative Reasoning – MATH 110 - PRECALCULUS (4)
- INTD 101 - FIRST YEAR SEMINAR (4)
- CRWT 102 - CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II (4)

**First Year, Spring Semester — total 16 credits** [1]
- CMPS 148 - COMPUTER SCIENCE II (4)
- MATH 121 - CALCULUS I (4)
- CMPS 220 - ASSEMBLY LANGUAGE PROGRAMMING (4)
- General Education Requirement * (4)
- PATH 001 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1

The complete recommended plan, including the remaining semesters, is at https://www.ramapo.edu/recommended-graduation-plan-2026/tas/computer-science/ [1]. Other plans for that year are Computer Science with MS in Applied Mathematics 4+1, Computer Science with MS in Computer Science 4+1, and Computer Science with MS in Data Science 4+1 [1]. Also published: Computer Science 4+1, Computer Science MS, and Computer Science Minor [1].

question: Is there a combined bachelor's and master's program where I could finish both degrees in five years, and which majors is it available for?

body.answer:
Yes. Ramapo lists two 4+1 options for completing a bachelor’s and master’s in five years [1][2][8].

- **Accounting 4+1:** Accounting BS and Accounting MS (MSAC). The program description says it is a five-year option and that graduate courses begin senior year, with completion in the fifth year [1]. Catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-PMSA. The listed undergraduate major is Accounting BS [3].
- **Computer Science 4+1:** Computer Science MS after a four-year bachelor’s, with the MS completed in one additional year. Designed for students in Computer Science BS, Data Science BS, and Mathematics BS; students in other disciplines may contact the Graduate Program Director about a five-year plan [2]. The three named majors are listed in the catalog [3]. Catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-PMCS.

To declare a 4+1, the Registrar says to contact the graduate program director for enrollment information and guidelines, then use the 4+1 Declaration Form: https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/04/41-Declaration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf [8]. Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7695 [8].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-PMSA) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-PMCS) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/forms-transcripts/)

question: Can you tell me which of my community college credits will transfer and how many credits I'll come in with?

body.answer:
Ramapo’s pages don’t identify which of your specific courses will transfer or how many credits you personally will receive; that requires reviewing your records. [3,5]

After acceptance, you’ll receive a Transfer Credit Worksheet showing the number of credits accepted. [3] Coursework needing review may be submitted to your major’s Convener or reviewed at orientation for more detailed course equivalency. [3]

If you’re transferring from a New Jersey community college with an A.A. or A.S., Ramapo says it accepts the full degree, up to the two-year-school maximum; AAS degrees and credits without an associate degree are evaluated course by course. [8] NJ county college course equivalencies and planning resources are at www.NJTransfer.org. [11]

For the maximum, the general transfer FAQ says up to 65 credits from an accredited community college. [9] Adult-student pages say a maximum of 64 credits from two-year institutions or community colleges. [10,12] The pages give different limits; which applies depends on your student category.

For help with your individual evaluation, contact Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7300. [3]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/agreements/)

question: I'm torn between majoring in communication arts and minoring in business, or majoring in business and minoring in communication. Which one would be better for getting a job in marketing?

body.answer:
The pages don’t say which combination is better for getting a marketing job, so I can’t verify a recommendation. They do describe the Marketing BS as preparing students for marketing-related careers including digital marketing, social media marketing, advertising, brand management and market research. Its curriculum includes marketing communication, consumer behavior, research and strategy. [1] The Marketing Minor requires MKTG 290, MKTG 310, MKTG 320, and two electives from its listed options. [2] Communication Arts is described as preparing students to apply writing, research and problem-solving skills in communication and media; its requirements vary by concentration. [3] The provided pages don’t establish the requirements or career outcomes for a Business major or Communication minor.

For help comparing the choices, the Cahill Career Development Center recommends connecting with faculty and speaking with a Career Advisor; FOCUS 2 can help explore careers and select a major (access code: ramapo430). [5][9] The Center for Student Success advises gathering information, talking with advisors and students, and considering a major with a minor; it notes that job experience matters and recommends co-op or internship experience. [11]

Contacts: Cahill Career Development Center, careercenter@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7444; ASB Office, (201) 684-7675. [5][9] Center for Student Success (Academic Advising), success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441. [11]
